intro: Every word this module’s exercises use, on one deck of flashcards: 365 cards, 184 of them nouns. The vocabulary of this module is precise, stylistically marked vocabulary: register pairs, legal and philosophical terms, and fixed expressions, from the themes Philosophie & Gesellschaft, Wissenschaftssprache, Recht & Verwaltung: Amtsdeutsch, Literatur: Lyrik & Deutung. Write the German, choose it from four options, or flip the card and rate yourself. A word you miss comes back later in the same run, and stays in your weak words until you get it right three times in a row.
tips[0].title: Register is part of the meaning
tips[0].text: Two words can mean the same and still not be interchangeable. The note on the back often names the plain or colloquial equivalent; learn which one fits a formal text.
tips[0].check.why: eine Vielzahl von is the formal choice; ein Haufen and ein Batzen are colloquial.
tips[1].title: Focus particles change what is stressed
tips[1].text: selbst, sogar, ausgerechnet, erst, nur, lediglich, zumindest, erst recht: each one points at one word and says how surprising, small or large it is.
tips[1].check.why: erst marks something as later than expected; nur marks it as less.
tips[2].title: Abstract nouns still have a gender
tips[2].text: die Vernunft, die Würde, das Gewissen, der Zweck, das Mittel: abstract ideas take der, die or das like any noun, and the ending is still the best clue.
tips[2].check.why: das Gewissen: a noun from a Ge-… stem, neuter.
remember[0]: Never say a noun without its article, not even in your head.
remember[1]: Miss a word? It comes back in the same run. Three correct answers in a row take it off the weak list.
remember[2]: Verbs and adjectives have no article: type them as they stand, like "selbst".
hook: Gather the precise words of philosophy, science, law and literature, each with its article and its register.
